chapter: On the road, Philadelphia and New York
title: Atlantic and Gotham repertoire; Sidewalks of New York in chords
summary: He confirms the repertoire and says Sidewalks of New York, in all chords, was an early experiment.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: The discography lists a lot of recordings for Atlantic and Gotham at that time. Are these typical of the tunes you played in clubs: Annie Laurie, Hot Harlem, Flying Home, Park Eyes, Sidewalks of New York.
There's a listing of a session with a singer named J.B. Summers, doing a tune called Drinkin' Beer.
- Drinkin' Beer? No. But as far as chord forming was concerned, that was is concerned, that was one of the first tunes I played, Sidewalks of New York, in all chords.

Yeah but I didn't pursue it, that was one particular tune I played and then the rest -- cause everybody was single-note, you know. Chords were all right if you were strummin' with a big band or somethin'.
